slides.title: Year 2 Is Heavier
slides.content: Common Year 2 pressures include: Final Major Projects. Employer Set Projects. Coursework. Industry placements. Progression plans. Future career decisions. The workload is expected to feel heavier than Year 1.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Year 2 Is Heavier'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Year 2 Is Heavier.

slides.title: Mental Health Still Moves
slides.content: The same wellbeing spectrum applies: Thriving Coping Struggling In Crisis The difference is that Year 2 students have already seen how their wellbeing changes under pressure. Recognising your own warning signs is important.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Mental Health Still Moves'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Mental Health Still Moves.

slides.title: Stress Often Looks Like Avoidance
slides.content: Examples include: Avoiding Final Major Project work. Delaying difficult tasks. Avoiding production sessions. Ignoring skill gaps. Putting off important decisions. Stress becomes more harmful when it remains switched on continuously.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Stress Often Looks Like Avoidance'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Stress Often Looks Like Avoidance.

slides.title: The Same Four Solutions Still Work
slides.content: The evidence remains the same: Move. Connect. Sleep. Talk. These are maintenance habits, not personality traits.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'The Same Four Solutions Still Work'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on The Same Four Solutions Still Work.

slides.title: Sleep Matters More Than Students Think
slides.content: A tired brain: Learns less effectively. Makes poorer decisions. Finds projects harder. Experiences stronger emotions. Sleep directly supports final-year success.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Sleep Matters More Than Students Think'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Sleep Matters More Than Students Think.

slides.title: The Year 2 Support Paradox
slides.content: A common problem: The year students most need support is often the year they stop using it. Many Year 2 students feel they should already be able to cope independently. This is often the wrong assumption.

exercise.prompt: What is a key message of 'The Year 2 Support Paradox'?
options: It is only assessed in exams
A common problem: The year students most need support is often the year they stop using it
It applies only to certain students
It is optional and not required
exercise.explanation: A common problem: The year students most need support is often the year they stop using it

slides.title: Tell College About Changes
slides.content: If anything has changed since Year 1, such as: Health. Home circumstances. Mental health. Learning support needs. Tell the college early so support can be adjusted.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Tell College About Changes'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Tell College About Changes.

slides.title: Peer Responsibility Matters More
slides.content: Year 2 students know each other better. You are often the first person to notice: Withdrawal. Missed sessions. Changes in behaviour. Falling behind. Isolation. Notice, Ask, Tell remains the correct approach.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Peer Responsibility Matters More'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Peer Responsibility Matters More.

slides.title: Strong Finishes Need Early Support
slides.content: Students who seek support early are more likely to: Complete projects successfully. Address technical gaps. Manage workload effectively. Meet deadlines. Waiting until the end of the year often creates avoidable problems.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Strong Finishes Need Early Support'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Strong Finishes Need Early Support.

slides.title: Quick Revision Summary
slides.content: Key points to remember: Expect increased pressure Recognise your warning signs Avoid the trap of coping alone Continue using support services Look out for peers Seek help early to finish strongly. ,
